statement: Camellia visible-flower MRCA is reconstructed as white; flower-colour divergence involves TE/SV-linked regulatory rewiring and experimentally validated MYB60-associated anthocyanin suppression
evidence_or_result: 237 accessions / 129 species / 4,182,517 nuclear SNPs; regulatory mechanism demonstrated in source study
implication: provides a historical visible-state reference and a plausible regulatory route for suppression/reactivation
claim_ceiling: does not prove ancestral molecular latent state or branch-specific selection pressure

statement: Floral anthocyanin can be regained after evolutionary loss while core pathway genes remain conserved
evidence_or_result: Iochrominae studies report intact pathway coding regions through pigment losses and a candidate regain with renewed late-pathway expression
implication: reactivation/redeployment after loss is biologically plausible without reconstructing the whole pathway
claim_ceiling: not evidence that Camellia has the same history or selection pressure

statement: A genuine floral-colour regain can be coupled to pollinator reversal
evidence_or_result: Petunia secreta regained anthocyanin via a 2-bp reading-frame-restoring mutation in AN2 during reversal toward bee pollination
implication: pollinator-mediated selection can select a regained pigment programme
claim_ceiling: not evidence that Camellia reactivation is pollinator driven

statement: The same human-visible red state can encode different pollinator signals in Camellia
evidence_or_result: C. rusticana is bee-associated with UV reflectance/fluorescence whereas C. japonica is bird-associated and relatively inconspicuous to bees
implication: selection target can be spectral/UV phenotype rather than hue category
claim_ceiling: one species pair does not establish genus-wide frequency

statement: Weather-dependent pollinator reliability and strong bird contribution occur in a yellow Camellia
evidence_or_result: bird exclusion reduced fruit/seed set by 64%; honeybee visits declined in cloudy/rainy weather
implication: climate/weather can alter the relative reliability of pollinator functional groups
claim_ceiling: not a historical reactivation test

statement: Pollinator weighting can shift seasonally within one golden Camellia species
evidence_or_result: winter had higher bird visitation, fruit/seed set, nectar volume and sucrose ratio than summer
implication: supports climate/season -> pollinator-functional-environment coupling as a plausible selector
claim_ceiling: does not identify flower-colour evolution or reactivation

statement: Floral UV pigmentation can covary with altitude, temperature and UV-B across a clade
evidence_or_result: 177 Potentilleae species; larger UV-absorbing areas at higher altitude/lower temperature/higher UV exposure
implication: direct abiotic filtering of floral pigment is plausible in some clades
claim_ceiling: cannot be transferred as a universal Camellia mechanism

statement: Abiotic flower-colour associations can exist within species but disappear at macroevolutionary scale
evidence_or_result: within-species anthocyanin-environment associations; no phylogenetically corrected joint evolution of flower colour and environment across two radiations
implication: micro ecological response need not generate a macro trait-niche pattern
claim_ceiling: does not determine which filter acts in Camellia

statement: Camellia pigment deployment is repeatedly accessible through regulatory/flux changes
evidence_or_result: 8/8 independence clusters show regulatory/flux evidence; 6/6 informative clusters show higher anthocyanin in the more-red state
implication: variation generation is highly repeatable at the mechanistic scale
claim_ceiling: literature is selected/heterogeneous; not a natural transition-frequency estimate

statement: Human-visible anthocyanin-like A state does not generally occupy colder Camellia niches than W
evidence_or_result: provenance-clean A-W tests: BIO1 P=0.805; BIO6 median P=0.526; BIO6 q05 P=0.252; BIO1 IQR P=0.705
implication: direct genus-wide climate selection on redness is insufficient
claim_ceiling: lineage-specific abiotic effects remain possible

statement: W/A/Y visible states are not deterministic ecological-functional states
evidence_or_result: same-red C. japonica/C. rusticana differ in pollination/spectral function; same-yellow taxa differ in pollinator weighting; yellow biochemistry can mix flavonol and carotenoid axes
implication: selection-pressure tests should model latent biochemical/spectral states, not hue alone
claim_ceiling: latent-state superiority cannot yet be fitted because spectral/chemical data are sparse

statement: Anthocyanin-like A is far more section-concentrated than expected from its species count in the exact 50-species screen
evidence_or_result: A: 14 species in 2 sections vs 6.59279 expected under 100000 label shuffles; breadth lower-tail P=0.00003; entropy lower-tail P<0.00001
implication: macro persistence/deployment of A is lineage-gated despite high micro accessibility
claim_ceiling: traditional sections are a history proxy and the 50-species niche subset is not the full nuclear phylogeny

statement: White is not unusually section-broad after controlling for its larger sample size in the exact 50-species screen
evidence_or_result: W: 34 species in 9 sections vs 9.12673 expected; breadth lower-tail P=0.651; entropy lower-tail P=0.413
implication: raw 9/10-section occupancy cannot by itself establish white as an evolutionary hub/reservoir
claim_ceiling: latent-white hypothesis still has molecular-retention support and needs branch transition tests

statement: Apparent extreme niche shifts can be created by a few occurrence-provenance errors
evidence_or_result: four shared extreme-coordinate records shifted Tuberculatae BIO6 q05 by ~15.5-16.8 C and generated a spurious section cold-tail signal
implication: environmental events must be validated before selection-pressure attribution
claim_ceiling: demonstrated for one candidate; prevalence genus-wide remains unknown

statement: Current ecological evidence is much denser for pollinator regime than for spectral/biochemical selection targets
evidence_or_result: latent-state seed: pollinator 6/8 informative; anthocyanin 5/8; flavonol 4/8; UV/fluorescence 1/8; carotenoid 1/8
implication: next evidence gain should prioritize reflectance/UV and pigment chemistry rather than simply adding more climate points
claim_ceiling: 8-taxon seed is a prioritization audit, not a genus-level parameter estimate

statement: High molecular accessibility is filtered by lineage-specific permissivity, so easy pigment states become macro-persistent only in some historical/ecological backgrounds
evidence_or_result: generated by CHUN_MICRO_ACCESS + CHUN_A_SECTION_CONCENTRATION + strong full-table section-colour structure
implication: predicts enrichment of A gains/persistence in specific nuclear-tree backgrounds after transition opportunity is controlled
claim_ceiling: requires primary nuclear stochastic histories; section is not a phylogeny

statement: Selection acts more directly on biochemical/spectral latent phenotype than on human-visible W/A/Y hue
evidence_or_result: generated by CHUN_STATE_ALIASING and weak provenance-clean hue-climate prediction
implication: predicts latent pigment/spectral models outperform hue labels for pollinator/niche persistence
claim_ceiling: not testable at genus scale until UV/carotenoid/chemical gaps are reduced

statement: Adaptive reactivation can be an enabler or a follower; the causal distinction is determined by event ordering
evidence_or_result: generated by strong molecular accessibility but null present-day A-W climate association
implication: compare environment-first -> reactivation, reactivation-first -> niche expansion, pollinator-first -> reactivation and synchronous histories
claim_ceiling: no branch-specific Camellia reactivation has yet passed the historical/molecular gate

statement: Climate may select colour re-deployment indirectly by altering pollinator reliability/seasonality rather than by direct floral stress tolerance
evidence_or_result: generated by genus-wide direct-cold null plus source-level C. petelotii weather response and C. perpetua seasonal pollinator shift
implication: predicts climate -> pollinator-regime -> latent spectral/pigment transition fits better than climate -> hue alone
claim_ceiling: currently plausible mechanism, not a Camellia macroevolutionary conclusion

statement: Some apparent reactivations restore a previously useful signal when an ancestral-like ecological/pollinator regime recurs rather than enabling a genuinely novel niche
evidence_or_result: generated by retained-pathway accessibility plus known pollinator-linked regain examples outside Camellia and state-function collisions within Camellia
implication: compare ecological distance of post-reactivation regime to pre-loss ancestral regime versus genuinely novel occupied climates/pollinators
claim_ceiling: requires dated nuclear histories and reconstructed ecological regimes
